spec.description:
How Karpenter adds, replaces and removes the cluster's nodes on EKS.

Launches and their errors, capacity EC2 refused, how long nodes take to join, what keeps nodes from being consolidated, and the controller's health. The cloud-agnostic view is Infrastructure Autoscaling.

**AWS API calls that did not succeed per minute, by service, action and status.**

**Nominal:** A trickle of `400` on `DescribeLaunchTemplates`, which is Karpenter looking for a launch template before it creates it.

**Degraded:** `403` is a permission Karpenter's IAM role lacks; `429` or `RequestLimitExceeded` is API throttling, often from something else in the account. `CreateFleet` errors are launches EC2 refused; the Provisioning tab's _EC2 Errors_ says why.

`412` is left out: EC2 answers every dry run with it, and Karpenter dry runs `CreateFleet` and `RunInstances` to check its EC2NodeClasses. The SDK's own `service` label arrives as `exported_service`, since the scrape stamps the Kubernetes Service name on `service`.
spec.title: Failed AWS Calls per Minute

defaults.noValue: No failed AWS calls

spec.description:
**CPU each Karpenter replica uses, in cores.**

The standby replica uses almost none.
spec.title: CPU by Replica

defaults.noValue: No metrics: cadvisor metrics are required (via kubelet)

spec.description:
**Kubernetes API calls that did not succeed per minute, by method and status.**

**Nominal:** Near zero. `409` conflicts are an object changed underneath Karpenter, which it retries.

**Degraded:** `429` is the API server throttling Karpenter; `5xx` an API server in trouble, which also shows as _Cluster State Synced_ dropping.
spec.title: Failed Kubernetes API Calls per Minute

defaults.noValue: No failed Kubernetes API calls

spec.description:
**Which Karpenter replica holds the leader lease.**

Only the leader provisions and disrupts. A change of leader restarts its counters, and Karpenter spends a few seconds syncing its state.
spec.title: Leader

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Memory each Karpenter replica holds, against its limit.**

**Degraded:** The leader near its limit. Karpenter's memory grows with the number of nodes, pods and instance types it tracks, and an out-of-memory restart stops all provisioning while the standby takes over.
spec.title: Memory by Replica

defaults.noValue: No metrics: cadvisor and kube-state-metrics are required

options.content:
**Karpenter is not reporting on this cluster.**

Karpenter adds nodes on EKS in the self-managed Terraform. GKE and AKS use their managed cluster autoscaler instead, which has no equivalent of this dashboard: **Infrastructure Autoscaling** covers every cloud.

On EKS, this dashboard needs the ServiceMonitor that the Terraform `karpenter` module creates with `enable_service_monitor`, and the monitoring CRDs installed before Karpenter, which the examples' `monitoring-crds` module does. Karpenter's chart leaves the ServiceMonitor out when the CRDs are not there yet, and does not add it later on its own; re-apply once they are.

spec.description:
**Reconcile errors per minute, by controller.**

**Nominal:** Near zero. A few are routine: an object changed while it was being reconciled, and the next attempt succeeds.

**Degraded:** A controller erroring steadily. Its log lines, on the Events and Logs tab, carry the error.
spec.title: Reconcile Errors per Minute

defaults.noValue: No reconcile errors

spec.description:
**Items waiting in each of Karpenter's work queues.**

**Nominal:** Near zero.

**Degraded:** A queue that grows and does not drain: that controller is behind.
spec.title: Work Queue Depth

defaults.noValue: Every queue is empty

spec.expr:
sum by (why) (
  count_over_time(
    {job="loki.source.kubernetes_events"}
      | reportingcontroller="karpenter"
      | reason=~"DisruptionBlocked|Unconsolidatable"
      | line_format "{{.msg}}"
      | regexp "^(?P<why>Pod has .karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt. annotation|Pdb prevents pod evictions|NodePool .[^ ]+. has [a-z-]+ consolidation disabled|[A-Z][^(]+)"
  [5m])
)

spec.description:
**Why Karpenter is leaving nodes in place, from its `DisruptionBlocked` and `Unconsolidatable` events per five minutes.**

**Nominal:** On a Materialize cluster, mostly the `do-not-disrupt` annotation: the operator marks every Materialize pod so, because moving a replica means rehydrating it. That is the design working, not a fault.

**Degraded:** A PodDisruptionBudget blocking the same pods for hours holds nodes that could otherwise be removed or replaced, including drifted nodes that should be.

Karpenter repeats these events every few minutes for every blocked node, so the numbers track how long, not how many.
spec.title: Why Disruption Is Blocked

defaults.noValue: No blocked disruptions in this time range

spec.description:
**Karpenter's blocked-disruption events, newest first.**

The message names the pod or PodDisruptionBudget holding each node.
spec.title: Blocked Disruption Events

defaults.noValue: No blocked disruptions in this time range

spec.description:
**Nodes each NodePool's disruption budget allows removing right now, by reason.**

Zero is a budget that allows none at the moment, by design or because nodes are already being disrupted.
spec.title: Disruptions the Budget Allows

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Disruptions Karpenter decided on per hour, by reason and action.**

`delete` removes a node whose pods fit elsewhere; `replace` launches a cheaper or up-to-date node first.
spec.title: Disruption Decisions per Hour

defaults.noValue: No disruption decisions

spec.description:
**NodeClaims removed or replaced per hour, by NodePool and reason.**

`empty` and `underutilized` are consolidation; `drifted` a node that no longer matches its NodePool or EC2NodeClass, such as after an AMI update; `expired` one past its NodePool's `expireAfter`; `interrupted` one AWS is reclaiming.
spec.title: NodeClaims Disrupted per Hour

defaults.noValue: No nodes disrupted

spec.description:
**Nodes Karpenter considers candidates for disruption, by reason.**

Candidates stay candidates while something blocks them. A count that stays high while _NodeClaims Disrupted_ stays at zero is a blocked disruption; _Why Disruption Is Blocked_ says by what.
spec.title: Nodes Eligible for Disruption

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Pod evictions Karpenter requested per minute, by response.**

**Nominal:** Mostly `200`, the eviction allowed.

**Degraded:** `429` is an eviction a PodDisruptionBudget refused. Karpenter retries, and the node is not removed until the budget allows it.
spec.title: Eviction Requests per Minute

defaults.noValue: No evictions requested

spec.description:
**Notices Karpenter read from its interruption queue per hour, by type.**

`spot_interrupted` and `rebalance_recommendation` apply to Spot capacity, which the examples do not use. `scheduled_change` is AWS maintenance on a host, and `instance_stopped` or `instance_terminated` an instance stopped outside Karpenter. The queue receives every instance event in the account and region, so `no_op`, an event about an instance that is not Karpenter's, is usually most of it.
spec.title: Interruption Notices per Hour

defaults.noValue: No interruption notices

**Each of Karpenter's nodes, with its NodePool, instance type, zone and age.**

spec.description:
**How long notices waited in the interruption queue before Karpenter read them, at the 99th percentile over the last hour.**

**Nominal:** Seconds.

**Unhealthy:** Minutes: Karpenter is not keeping up, or was down. A notice read late leaves less of AWS's warning to drain the node in.
spec.title: Notice Wait in Queue (p99)

defaults.noValue: No interruption notices in the last hour

spec.description:
**How long NodeClaims took to terminate, from the decision to the instance gone, at the 99th percentile over the last hour.**

**Degraded:** Hours: pods that could not be evicted held the node. Nodes in the Materialize pool wait for a Materialize rollout to move their pods.
spec.title: Time to Terminate a Node (p99)

defaults.noValue: No nodes terminated in the last hour

spec.description:
**Consolidation searches that ran out of time, per hour.**

Karpenter gives up on a search and tries again later; frequent timeouts mean consolidation rarely completes on a large cluster.
spec.title: Consolidation Timeouts per Hour

spec.description:
**Every condition on each NodePool and EC2NodeClass, and its current status.**

**Nominal:** Every row True.

**Unhealthy:** A False or Unknown row, with its reason. On an EC2NodeClass, `AMIsReady`, `SubnetsReady`, `SecurityGroupsReady` or `InstanceProfileReady` false means Karpenter cannot build a launch request at all. On a NodePool, `NodeRegistrationHealthy` false means instances launched but did not join the cluster.
spec.title: NodePool and NodeClass Conditions

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**NodeClaims Karpenter removed or replaced in the selected time range, in the selected NodePools.**

Consolidation, drift, expiry and interruption all count. A Materialize replica on a disrupted node restarts elsewhere, so a Materialize pool should read low; the examples mark its pods not to be disrupted, which is why it usually reads zero.
spec.title: Nodes Disrupted (Select Time Range)

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Instance launches EC2 refused in the selected time range.**

**Nominal:** Zero.

**Unhealthy:** Any. Karpenter retries with another instance type or zone where the NodePool allows one; a NodePool with a single instance type, like the Terraform examples' Materialize pool, has nowhere else to go. The error type on the Provisioning tab says whether it was capacity, quota or a configuration problem.
spec.title: Launch Errors (Select Time Range)

spec.description:
**NodePools that are not Ready.**

**Nominal:** Zero.

**Unhealthy:** A NodePool that is not Ready launches nothing. Its conditions in _NodePool and NodeClass Conditions_ say why: usually its EC2NodeClass cannot find an AMI, subnet or security group, or `NodeRegistrationHealthy` is false because the nodes it launched never joined the cluster.
spec.title: NodePools Not Ready

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Nodes Karpenter manages, in the selected NodePools.**

Nodes from an EKS managed node group, such as the base group Karpenter itself runs on, are not Karpenter's and are left out.
spec.title: Nodes

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description: **Karpenter's nodes in each NodePool over time.**
spec.title: Nodes by NodePool

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Whether Karpenter's view of the cluster's nodes and pods is in step with Kubernetes.**

**Nominal:** 1, synced.

**Unhealthy:** 0 for more than a few seconds. Karpenter makes no scheduling or disruption decision until it is back in step, so pods wait and nodes are not removed. Usually an API server problem; the Controller tab has the error rates.
spec.title: Cluster State

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**Pods Karpenter could not find or create a node for in its last scheduling pass.**

**Nominal:** Zero.

**Unhealthy:** Non-zero for more than a pass or two: no NodePool can hold these pods. Their node selectors, affinities or tolerations match no pool, a pool is at its limits, or no instance type in the pool is big enough. The pods' `FailedScheduling` events, on Infrastructure Autoscaling, name the constraint.
spec.title: Pods Karpenter Cannot Place

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**The share of Karpenter's nodes' allocatable CPU, memory and pod slots that pods have requested.**

**Nominal:** High. Karpenter consolidates onto fewer nodes when it can, so a low reading that stays low means something is keeping it from doing so.

**Degraded:** Low and not recovering. The Disruption tab says what is blocking consolidation; on a Materialize cluster it is usually replicas marked not to be disrupted.
spec.title: Requested Share of Karpenter's Nodes

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description: **The Karpenter version running.**
spec.title: Version

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**How long Karpenter's calls to AWS take, by operation, at the 99th percentile.**

`Create` is a launch, which waits on EC2; `GetInstanceTypes` refreshes the catalogue and prices.
spec.title: AWS Call Duration (p99)

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**NodeClaims created per hour, by NodePool and reason.**

`provisioned` is a new node for waiting pods; `drifted`, `expired` and the consolidation reasons are replacements.
spec.title: NodeClaims Created per Hour

defaults.noValue: No NodeClaims created

spec.description:
**Errors from EC2 per hour, by error type and operation.**

**Nominal:** Nothing on `Create`.

**Unhealthy:** On `Create`: `InsufficientCapacityError` is EC2 out of the instance type in a zone, which Karpenter works around if the NodePool allows other types or zones. `UnfulfillableCapacity` and quota errors need a change on the AWS side, and the others usually a change to the EC2NodeClass.

`NodeClaimNotFoundError` on `Delete` or `IsDrifted` is an instance already gone when Karpenter checked on it, which is routine after a termination.
spec.title: EC2 Errors per Hour

defaults.noValue: No errors from EC2

options.content:
**Karpenter is not reporting on this cluster.**

Karpenter adds nodes on EKS in the self-managed Terraform. GKE and AKS use their managed cluster autoscaler instead, which has no equivalent of this dashboard: **Infrastructure Autoscaling** covers every cloud.

On EKS, this dashboard needs the ServiceMonitor that the Terraform `karpenter` module creates with `enable_service_monitor`, and the monitoring CRDs installed before Karpenter, which the examples' `monitoring-crds` module does. Karpenter's chart leaves the ServiceMonitor out when the CRDs are not there yet, and does not add it later on its own; re-apply once they are.

spec.description:
**Zones where each of the node pools' instance types can be launched, by capacity type.**

**Nominal:** Flat.

**Degraded:** A dip: EC2 refused a launch for capacity, and Karpenter stops asking that zone for that type for a few minutes. A dip in the only type a NodePool allows is a pool that cannot grow in that zone until it recovers.

Only the types the Terraform's `service_monitor_instance_types` names are kept. Reserved capacity is left out: it reads unavailable wherever there is no reservation.
spec.title: Instance Type Availability

defaults.noValue: No availability data. The Terraform karpenter module keeps it only for service_monitor_instance_types.

spec.description:
**Pods waiting for Karpenter: the ones it cannot place, and the queue for its next scheduling pass.**

**Nominal:** Zero, or briefly non-zero while a node launches.
spec.title: Pods Waiting for Karpenter

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**How long each of Karpenter's scheduling passes takes, at the 99th percentile.**

**Nominal:** Well under a second.

**Degraded:** Seconds or more: a very large number of waiting pods or instance types to consider. Every pass delays the next node.
spec.title: Scheduling Pass Duration (p99)

defaults.noValue: Karpenter has not reported this yet.

spec.description:
**How long NodeClaims took to reach each stage of launching, at the 99th percentile over the last hour.**

`Launched` is EC2 accepting the request, `Registered` the node joining the cluster, and `Initialized` the node Ready with its startup taints removed. A slow `Registered` is usually the node's bootstrap; a missing one is a node that never joined.
spec.title: Node Launch Stages (p99)

defaults.noValue: No NodeClaims launched in the last hour

spec.description:
**How long pods that needed a new node took to start running, from when the scheduler gave up on existing nodes.**

**Nominal:** A minute or two: the time to launch an instance, boot it and join the cluster.

**Degraded:** Much longer, or rising: slow EC2 capacity, a slow AMI, or a node that joins but is slow to become Ready. _Node Launch Stages_ says which stage.
spec.title: Time for a Pod to Start on a New Node

defaults.noValue: No pods needed a new node in the last hour
